CC.US.02 HPV positive.precondition: Client was treated or deferred to follow-up after HPV-positive triage.
CC.US.02 HPV positive.trigger_event: Post-treatment or post-triage follow-up is due.
CC.US.02 HPV positive.user_action: Schedule and perform follow-up according to the pathway: re-test after 12 months for HPV-positive women with no lesion on colposcopy/VIA; post-treatment re-test with HPV after 12 months; if negative, return to routine screening; if still positive, repeat colposcopy; if suspicious for cancer, refer for evaluation, biopsy, and appropriate center management.
CC.US.02 HPV positive.system_response: System schedules follow-up, records results, and routes the client to routine screening, repeat colposcopy, retreatment, or referral as indicated.
CC.US.02 HPV positive.alternate_or_exception_path: If the follow-up test is positive, re-treat with LEEP (preferred) or cone biopsy; if suspected cancer, refer immediately.
CC.US.02 HPV positive.notes: This step captures the follow-up branches explicitly described for HPV-positive clients and post-treatment surveillance.

_provenance.evidence_excerpt: Women who test positive for hrHPV but have no lesion on colposcopy/VIA should re-test in 12 months; if still positive, repeat colposcopy
The first follow-up visit should be scheduled 1 year after treatment where re-testing is done preferably with HPV test

CC.US.03 VIA screen-treat.precondition: Acetic acid has been applied and the waiting interval has elapsed.
CC.US.03 VIA screen-treat.trigger_event: Provider interprets cervical appearance after acetic acid application.
CC.US.03 VIA screen-treat.user_action: Inspect the cervix for acetowhite changes and determine whether the result is positive or negative.
CC.US.03 VIA screen-treat.system_response: System stores VIA result and interpretation details.
CC.US.03 VIA screen-treat.alternate_or_exception_path: If acetowhite changes are seen in the transformation zone with well-defined borders, classify as positive; if no persistent acetowhite changes are noted, classify as negative.
CC.US.03 VIA screen-treat.notes: The one-minute waiting time is intended to allow faint inflammatory or metaplastic whitening to recede before interpretation.

_provenance.evidence_excerpt: Acetowhite changes on the cervix indicate likely cervical pre-cancer or cancer.
If these changes are seen in the transformation zone and have well-defined borders, they are considered a positive result.
If no persistent acetowhite changes are noted, then it is a negative result.
The one-minute waiting time allows for any areas that became faintly white due to inflammation or physiological cell changes (metaplasia) to recede.

_derivation.explanation: Combined the interpretation criteria and documentation requirement into one atomic VIA result step.
